question: The average of three numbers is 23. If two numbers are 11 and 25, the third number is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **average** (23) as the baseline for all numbers.

Deviation of 11 = 11 − 23 = −12

Deviation of 25 = 25 − 23 = +2

Net deviation of given numbers = −12 + 2 = −10

To maintain the **average**, the third number must balance this by being +10 from the average.

Third number = 23 + 10 = 33

**∴ The correct answer is 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of **three numbers** = 23

First number = 11

Second number = 25

**Formula:**

Sum of observations = **Average** × **Total number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10a609c572b018c9f858e7aa7f463c0aa5d93252de823a0863411e7f428a227e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of three numbers = 23 × 3 = 69

⇒ Sum of the two known numbers = 11 + 25 = 36

⇒ Third number = Total Sum − (Sum of two numbers)

⇒ Third number = 69 − 36

⇒ Third number = 33

**&there4$ The correct answer is 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Average

The sum of the **deviations** of all observations from their **mean (average)** is always zero. This is a powerful tool for finding missing values in a dataset.

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For a set of **n consecutive numbers** or numbers in an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the average is simply (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Effect of Change

If every number in a set is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant 'k', the **average** of the set also changes by the same constant 'k'.</p
